title: What is known about 1RB0RF_0LC---_1LD1LC_1RE0LA_1RA1RD_0RD0RF
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0RF_0LC---_1LD1LC_1RE0LA_1RA1RD_0RD0RF.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. Lean proves the word conversions for levels 1 to 3 (D going right turns 011(01)3k into 100 16k, C going left turns it back for k = 1, 2) and the 3-cell shifts. The behaviour of the boundaries between levels, where new levels are made, was not derived.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (B1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: Word conversions at each level
claims.text: For k = 1, 2, 3: D> (011(01)3k)n → (100 16k)n D> in (6k+5)n steps; for k = 1, 2: (0 16k+1 0)n C> 1 → C> 1 (011(01)3k)n; and the 3-cell shifts D> (011)n → (100)n D>, (100)n D> 1 → D> 1 (110)n, E> (110)n → (001)n E>.

claims.title: Where it can halt
claims.text: Only B reading 1 halts; B is entered only from A reading 0 (1RB), so the machine halts exactly on A> 0 1. Read off the table.

claims.title: The tape over time
claims.text: Runs of period 3, 9, 15, 21, 27, 33 from left to right: at 2.5·108 (100)1347 (111110011)243 ... (111111111110011)398 ... A> ... (21-cell)38; at 4·109 (100)8078 (9)662 (15)1624 (21)135 (27)323 (33)17 ... followed by a slowly growing right part of (111)m 011011(01)j blocks.

claims.title: A bouncer whose zones are levels
claims.text: The head sweeps the whole level structure; each pass converts the words of the level it crosses between dense and sparse form, and the boundaries between levels move, so the counts of each level rise and fall. The highest level present grows slowly (5 levels at 4·10<sup>9</sup> steps). Observed only.

claims.title: No closed tape language with small windows
claims.text: bbtools.ctl K = 3..6 leaves halting configurations; n-gram CPS fails; no invariant mod 2..12.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 35,340 cells have been visited and 19,249 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: exp/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.504). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.11).

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The machine stops only on A> 0 1; inside a run of one level the proved conversions never produce it, so the question is about the boundaries between levels and the right end, where new levels form; their rules were not derived.

claims.title: Related holdouts
claims.text: The same table as 1RB1RE_1RC0RF_0LD---_1LE1LD_1RA0LB_0RE0RF up to renaming, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each. The same table as 1RB1RA_1LC0RD_1LD1LB_1LE0LF_0RA---_0LB0LF up to renaming and mirroring, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each. The same table as 1RB0LC_1RC1RA_1RD0RF_0LE---_1LA1LE_0RA0RF up to renaming, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each. The same tapes at another pace, whatever the states, as 2 other holdouts (listed on the explainer page).

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Started on a blank tape, this Turing machine has run for 10<sup>9</sup> steps without stopping. This page runs the real machine in your browser, shows the shape of its run, and lists what is known, each result marked by what it rests on.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator; 35,340 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
The growth shape of the two sides of the tape (see below).

sections.heading: Runs of words of length 9, 15, 21, ...
html: At step 4·109 the tape, read left to right, is a run of 100 (8,078 copies), then runs of 9-cell words (662), 15-cell words (1,624), 21-cell words (135), 27-cell words (323), 33-cell words (17), and a right part of (111)m 011011(01)j blocks. The run of level k is made of words of length 6k + 3.
Each word comes in two forms: dense, 100 16k (nearly all 1s), and sparse, 011 (01)3k (alternating). Left of the head the words are dense, right of it sparse.

sections.heading: D makes words dense, C makes them sparse
html: Lean proves, for levels 1 to 3, that D going right turns each sparse word into the dense one in 6k + 5 steps per word, and (for levels 1 and 2) that C going left turns the dense word back. So the head is a bouncer that flips the form of the words as it passes. What happens where two levels meet, and how a new level is made at the right end, was not derived.

sections.heading: Only on A> 0 1
html: Only B reading 1 stops the machine, and B is reached only from A reading 0 and stepping right, so it stops exactly when A stands on 0 1. The proved conversions never produce that inside a run; it could only happen at a boundary between levels.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.504). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.11).
After 109 steps the tape spans 35,340 cells (24,045 left of the start, 498 right), with a density of 1s of 0.545.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machines below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in any of the others, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

  • 1RB1RE_1RC0RF_0LD---_1LE1LD_1RA0LB_0RE0RF: rename A→B, B→C, C→D, D→E, E→A, F→F; it is this table started in state E
  • 1RB1RA_1LC0RD_1LD1LB_1LE0LF_0RA---_0LB0LF: rename A→D, B→E, C→A, D→B, E→C, F→F and exchange left and right; it is this table started in state C, in a mirror
  • 1RB0LC_1RC1RA_1RD0RF_0LE---_1LA1LE_0RA0RF: rename A→C, B→D, C→E, D→A, E→B, F→F; it is this table started in state D

Same tapes at another pace (observed, not proved). Leave the states aside and compare only the tape and the place of the head. Then a large part of the first 107 configurations of this machine are configurations of the machines below, in the same order and up to the end of the run. The steps at which they occur differ, the tables are not renamings of each other, and equal tapes with different states may be continued differently, so this does not tie the halting questions together.

  • 1RB0LE_1RC1RB_1LD0RA_1LA1LC_0LC1LF_0RA--- (in a mirror): 8,003,899 configurations, the last at step 9,999,998 here and step 8,007,428 there
  • 1RB0LE_1RC1RB_1LD0RE_1LA1LC_1RB0LF_0LC--- (in a mirror): 8,003,899 configurations, the last at step 9,999,998 here and step 8,003,898 there

summary: A bouncer of runs at growing levels: level k is a run of (6k+3)-cell words, dense 100 1^(6k) on one side of the head and sparse 011 (01)^(3k) on the other; D going right makes them dense, C going left makes them sparse, and new levels appear slowly on the right.
